newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin to respect Chirac constitutional role.
newsitem.headline: Jospin to respect Chirac constitutional role.

text.p: French Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin promised on Thursday to respect the constitutional prerogatives of conservative President Jacques Chirac under left-right power sharing, Chirac's spokeswoman said.

"The prime minister has committed himself to respect the high constitutional prerogatives of the president," Catherine Colonna told reporters after a first cabinet meeting. The constitution gives the president a major role in foreign affairs and defence but gives the government control of domestic policy.

She said Jospin, swept to power in an upset parliamentary election victory on Sunday, would work with Chirac "calmly and with the rigour that befits the conduct of the nation's affairs, beyond political differences".

Jospin and Chirac made a respectful start to France's third 'cohabitation' at the brief cabinet meeting. The late Socialist president Francois Mitterrand shared power with centre-right governments from 1986-88 and 1993-95.

The 1958 constitution, which is unclear on the division of responsibilities, makes the president the guarantor of national independence and respect for international treatites, and head of the armed forces. But it also says "the government determines and carries out the nation's policy" and makes the prime minister "responsible for national defence".

Government spokeswoman Catherine Trautmann said Jospin told ministers they should uphold "the impartiality of the state" and that a change of political majority did not mean an upheaval in the civil service.
